key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings improved titanium wear resistance, with O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3 delivering the best reported tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing the spray gas ratio could improve the durability of hydroxyapatite-coated titanium implants under physiological wear conditions.
method: Deposited hydroxyapatite on Grade 2 titanium at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 2.6–3.7.
Used X-ray diffraction to identify hydroxyapatite and partial α-tricalcium phosphate formation.
Evaluated friction and wear under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved wear resistance versus uncoated titanium and the lowest wear volumes at ratios of 3.0 and 3.3, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Long-term coating integrity and biological osseointegration require validation beyond the reported tribological tests.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
